newsitem.title: UK: LME copper just firmer after upside attempt fails.
newsitem.headline: LME copper just firmer after upside attempt fails.

text.p: Base metal prices meandered within narrow ranges on Thursday, and traders said volumes were thin and trading uninspired.
Three months copper was arguably the biggest mover of the day, clambering up nearly to the $2,280 per tonne level early in the day.
But the market was reluctant to stay at the highs and prices finished the afternoon kerb at $2,260, just $4 up from Wednesday's close.
Copper had similarly failed an upside stab on Wednesday, when it slid lower after touching $2,293.

"Things petered out in the afternoon, the same as yesterday. But copper may be getting a bit oversold so if the market is getting a bit short prices could pick up tomorrow ahead of the weekend," a trader said.
Spreads were largely ignored and cash to threes backwardation was just narrower at $32/$33.
Chartwise, copper looked to be consolidating after last week's sharp fund sell-off, and traders said they did not expect prices to move significantly in the near term.
The other metals showed even less spark and mostly finished little changed after trading in tiny bands.
Aluminium was barely firmer at $1,550, up $3 from Wednesday's kerb close.
"A lot of the metals may need to drift down another $10-$15 before they can try the upside again," a trader said.
Lead and zinc were very quiet most of the day, but during the kerb some aggressive selling pushed them lower before a subsequent bounce.
Zinc ended $2 higher at $1,243, while lead was $5 lower at $634.
The market took note of news that Gold Fields Namibia's Tsumeb recently commissioned lead smelter would be closed for several weeks due to post-commissioning problems.
Tin was even more sluggish, barely budging most of the day. It finished just $5 lower at $5,685.
Nickel mimicked copper in trying the upside, but also failed above the $7,300 level and settled little changed.
It ended the kerb at $7,270, up$15.
Alloy was extremely quiet and was last indicated at $1,444/45, versus $1,448/50.
